name: lpc21isp
desc: In-circuit programming (ISP) tool for several NXP microcontrollers
why: Flashes NXP microcontrollers over serial via ISP; a real hardware door, though fairly niche and mundane in function.

brief.what_it_is: lpc21isp is a portable command-line in-circuit programming (ISP) tool for NXP LPC microcontrollers. The SourceForge page lists the LPC800, LPC1100, LPC1200, LPC1300, LPC1700, LPC1800, LPC2000 and LPC4300 series (ARM7, Cortex-M0, M0+, M3 and M4). The GitHub README also names Analog Devices ADUC70xx chips. It is written in C and runs from a terminal. The pages I read do not show invocation syntax, so I cannot confirm the exact inputs (firmware image, serial port, options) or outputs beyond the general description of flashing a chip over a serial ISP connection.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes it as a "Portable command line ISP for NXP LPC family and Analog Devices ADUC70xx", which suggests the aim is a cross-platform programmer that does not depend on vendor IDE tooling. The author is Martin Maurer, with portions copyright Aeolus Development (2004).

commands_seen.context: Build command for Microsoft Visual Studio, run from a VC console after vcvars32.bat, in the unpacked source directory.
Build command with make and gcc on Linux, Cygwin or similar shells, in the unpacked source directory.
Alternative build command for systems where gmake and gcc are used instead of make.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew is the install path in the brew entry. The README covers building from source only: Microsoft VC 6/7, VS2008 or VS2010 via nmake with Makefile.vc, or GCC on Cygwin, Linux or ARM ELF via Makefile.gnu. I did not see hardware wiring, serial port setup, bootloader entry steps or first-run configuration in the pages I read.
brief.standout: It is a single portable C command-line programmer that covers many LPC generations and several toolchains, including MSVC, Cygwin/Linux GCC and ARM ELF GCC. The SourceForge listing also points to GLPC, a GUI front-end built on top of it.
brief.status: Quiet. The SourceForge page shows its last update as 2015-10-06 and the README copyright runs through 2013. I found no recent release or commit activity, so I cannot call it actively maintained.
brief.caveats: Licence conflict: the SourceForge page says LGPLv2, but the README header says LGPL version 3 or later (and mentions GPL). Check the source before relying on either. The README gives only build instructions and no usage examples. The SourceForge page has few reviews (3 ratings), and the newest series listed are from around 2015. The README mentions old MSVC versions (6/7) and Cygwin, so some build paths may be dated.
